data.narrative:
ARC Clean Technology, founded by Don Wolf, is a Series G nuclear energy company that has raised $50M+ to date. The valuation universe consists of 8 comparable companies—3 public (Oklo, Nano Nuclear Energy, and SMR) and 5 private peers (Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Valar Atomics)—all operating in the nuclear energy sector.

The analysis applies a single triangulation method: stage-progression analysis. This method uses a $392.0B base value derived from the total-raised proxy and applies a typical Series G-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.25x, yielding an implied valuation of $490.0B. The peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables; while four same-sector peers exist, none met the threshold of three or more datapoints within matching stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier filters. A falling-back to all-sector medians risked introducing undue noise.

The triangulated valuation range spans $416.5B (low) to $563.5B (high), with a median of $490.0B. This single-method result carries material uncertainty, particularly around the appropriateness of the 1.25x step-up multiplier for a pre-commercial nuclear technology company and the reliability of the $50M+ raised figure as a proxy for intrinsic value. Obtaining additional comparable transaction data or revenue-based multiples, should they become available, would materially strengthen confidence in this range.
